$comment: Per-site login recipes (Cofre F-3). FIXED DATA — never model-authored, never user-authored, never fetched at runtime. Loaded by api/src/automation/login-recipes.ts and validated on load: every value must be a plain CSS selector, and the loader REFUSES the whole file rather than a single bad entry (a half-loaded registry is a registry nobody can reason about). Keys are eTLD+1-ish hosts matched the same way origin binding matches them, so a subdomain inherits its parent's recipe.
$loginUrlsComment: WHERE THE PASSWORD IS AIMED, as fixed reviewed data. A selector decides which field on a page receives the credential; the URL decides which HOST receives it, which is the strictly more dangerous of the two, and it was the one parameter left free-form at the caller. It is a SIBLING of `recipes` rather than a field inside a recipe entry on purpose: a recipe is selectors only ('a recipe may say WHERE the fields are, never what to do'), and a URL is not a selector — folding it in would blunt that rule and the loader validation that enforces it. The loader validates each entry as an https URL, with no userinfo, whose host is the key or a subdomain of it, so an entry here cannot aim one portal's password at another site. api/src/automation/session-establishment.ts PREFERS the URL declared here for a host and REFUSES a caller-supplied URL that disagrees with it.

citius.tribunaisnet.mj.pt.$note: Caixa Citius (Ministério da Justiça) — the tribunal portal the Cofre session-establishment path targets. Everything else about this portal (session lifetime, MFA behaviour, lock-out policy) is UNVERIFIED and must not be assumed.
